new_entities.name: Topical minoxidil 5%
new_entities.description: Topical 5% minoxidil formulations used for androgenetic alopecia.

edges.effect_quant: In a 48-week randomized trial of 393 men, 5% topical minoxidil outperformed both 2% minoxidil and placebo on nonvellus hair count and global scalp-coverage ratings. Later placebo-controlled foam studies and a head-to-head trial against oral minoxidil reinforce that topical 5% minoxidil remains a genuinely active hair-regrowth treatment.
edges.population: adult men with androgenetic alopecia using topical 5% minoxidil solution or foam over months
edges.mechanism: Topical minoxidil prolongs anagen and promotes follicular activity, improving hair density and slowing visible progression of male pattern hair loss.
edges.summary: Topical 5% minoxidil is one of the most established non-surgical male AGA treatments. It does not regrow a full juvenile hairline, but randomized evidence consistently shows better hair counts and coverage than placebo.
edges.caveats: Benefit depends on continued use and tends to be gradual. This edge is about meaningful improvement, not cure, and adherence or irritation issues can limit real-world outcomes.

evidence.citation: OlsenEA et al 2002 J Am Acad Dermatol
evidence.notes: A randomized clinical trial of 5% topical minoxidil versus 2% topical minoxidil and placebo in the treatment of androgenetic alopecia in men.

evidence.citation: OlsenEA et al 2007 J Am Acad Dermatol
evidence.notes: A multicenter, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial of a novel formulation of 5% minoxidil topical foam versus placebo in the treatment of androgenetic alopecia in men.
Oral Minoxidil vs Topical Minoxidil for Male Androgenetic Alopecia: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
